description: How an application reads a deployed graph, in both engines. The Java configuration reader normalizes a graph by flattening it to composite keys and rebuilding it; the Rust engine reproduces that for graphs (model_gate::normalize_graph). A null, an empty map and an empty list carry no value: a map drops such an entry, and a map or list that it leaves empty, while a list keeps such an element's place as null when an element with a value follows it and drops it at the end. An empty string is a value, and a dotted key becomes nested maps. Each engine writes 'input' to a file, reads it the way its startup compiler does and compares the result with 'expected'; 'gate' is what the deployment gate does with the result. Kept byte-identical in mercury-composable (system/minigraph-playground-engine/src/test/resources) and mercury (crates/knowledge-graph/tests/resources).
